Julius Sabinus and his wife Empona in the cave, surprised by the appearance of the Roman soldiers. " Sabinus was Commander of a small army in Gaul, and had declared himself Emperor upon the death of Vitellius. However, his army was shortly after overpowered by Vespasian's General, and he himself compelled to seek safety by flight. . . . He was obliged to hide himself in a cave ... for nine years, attended all the time by his wife Empona, who provided provisions for him by day, and repaired to him by night. However, she was at last discovered in the performance of this pious office, and Sabinus was taken prisoner and carried to Rome, where he was put to death by order of Vespasian."
